summary: The Paleobiology Database holds genus-level fossil occurrences with stratigraphic ages (the only source here covering richness through time), while living range and descendant data sit in separate resources (GBIF, Open Tree, TimeTree) that are not joined; a dominance measure and ancestor-to-descendant range links are not provided by any of them.
next_step: Define a dominance proxy (e.g. number of occupied equal-area cells from PBDB collection coordinates) for one well-sampled clade, pull its genus time series from PBDB, and pre-register the t to t+1 growth test.
obstacles_confirmed: Dominance has no single cross-taxon measure.
Abundance and dominance of ancestors are barely preserved, so descendant dominance is proxied by living range.
